title: Layer roles per copper-layer count (top to bottom). SIG = signals (with ground fill), GND = solid ground plane, PWR = power plane. 'alternatives' are accepted with apply --stackup and a stated reason.
rules: Fast signals run over a solid ground plane, never across a split or void in it; TI does not recommend referencing high-speed signals to a power plane [SPRAAR7J 2.4].

On four layers, signals outside and both inner layers ground is ADI's preferred option: fewer vias and advantages for switch-mode supplies; power goes as pours or wide tracks on the signal layers [ADI-EMI-4].

A power plane next to ground adds bypass capacitance only when the dielectric between them is thin: on JLC04161H-7628 the inner core is about 1.065 mm, about 3.8 pF/cm2 (derived: e0 x 4.6 / 1.065 mm), so it is negligible there.

2.source: (derived) from SPRAAR7J 2.4: with two layers the only reference a top-layer signal can have is a ground fill on the bottom layer, kept as unbroken as the routing allows.

4.source: ADI, Passing EMI Compliance Testing the First Time, Part 4: preferred 4-layer option, signals on the outer layers and ground on both inner layers. TI SPRAAR7J 2.4: no power-plane reference for high-speed signals.

alternatives.SIG,GND,PWR,SIG: TI SN75LVCP600S datasheet 11.1: ground next to the high-speed layer, power plane next to ground. The bottom layer then references the power plane: keep fast nets on the top layer. Use with a stated reason (a power plane is needed, or a thin inner core).

6.source: TI SPRAAR7J High-Speed Interface Layout Guidelines, Table 3-1 Example PCB Stackups (6-layer). The PWR layer is POWER/GROUND there; adjacent inner signal layers routed at 90 degrees to each other.

sources.SPRAAR7J: https://www.ti.com/lit/pdf/SPRAAR7 (revision J, February 2023), section 2.4 and Table 3-1
